newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens chip unit to triple sales by 2001.
newsitem.headline: Siemens chip unit to triple sales by 2001.

text.p: German industrial giant Siemens AG said on Thursday its semiconductor unit expected overseas expansion and strategic partnerships to nearly triple sales to around 14 billion marks ($8.3 billion) by 2001.

Siemens semiconductors (HL) forecast 26 percent annual sales growth over the next five years -- compared with a rate of 15 percent for the chip market as a whole during that time, HL chief executive Ulrich Schumacher told a news conference.
But growth in 1996/97 would be limited by sharp declines in chip prices over the last 15 months, he said.
"Siemens is banking on the semiconductor market reviving in the medium term," he said. "We have set a target of nearly trebling sales by 2001."

Most of the growth would come in Asia and the United States, where Siemens, the world's 12th-largest chip maker, forecast annual semiconductor market growth of 15 and 16 percent, respectively, between now and 2001.
To support international growth, Siemens plans to expand manufacturing capacity outside Germany and link up with other chip companies, he said.

"A worldwide presence, with manufacturing capacity on site and the move away from exports is only one step to making the semiconductor group a global player," he said. "Strategic alliances with other global players play a decisive role."
Siemens forecast chip market growth of six percent in 1997, accelerating to 18 percent in 1998 and 22 percent in 1999.

Chip pricing, which fell about 80 percent on some products in the past year, should stabilise next year as the Internet, expanding corporate networks, increasing use of mobile phones and wireless communications drive demand for semiconductors.

Falling prices caused HL net income to fall 24 percent to 603 million marks in the 1995/96 year to September 30. Previously, the unit had announced pre-tax profits of 603 million, making it the most profitable Siemens operation.

Sales last year grew only one percent in Germany and in the rest of Europe to 1.7 billion marks and 1.2 billion marks, respectively. North American sales rose 38 percent to 775 million marks and Asian sales gained 23 percent to 871 million.
In the three-month period that ended December 31, HL sales were down 12 percent at one billion marks. First quarter orders were down 24 percent at 1.2 billion marks.
HL's profit outlook was one of the main reasons Siemens forecast no improvement in overall group earnings for 1996/97.
